answer: Each seat leases one numbered burner on a mesa. At dawn the protocol issues a serialized dye capsule per seat and reveals its colour in that same block, so no plume can be filmed ahead of time. The seat must burn the capsule and let the plume rise ten minutes while two observers on a facing ridge photograph the tint. A capsule burns once and its serial dies, so cloning gains nothing: each extra identity needs another capsule, another leased burner, and two witnesses awake at that hour. A thousand fakes cost a thousand dawns of fuel and watcher fees, far above one seat’s settlement.
